scope: US-English RBY core plus approved UPR ZX 4.6.1; R/B full companion; Yellow trade-only
coverage_policy: Proof registrations must cite reviewed authoritative assertions and pin their implementation hash; test names and collection counts alone are not evidence. Empty proofs are explicit release blockers.

stages.description: Canonical sources, constants, structures, addresses, ROM layouts and generated data
Unit, server, admission, transaction, transport, DOM, route and API tests
Clean R/B/Y memory transformations and write-safe state gates
Real single-player engine behavior and every mandatory gameplay axis
Five live pairs: Red/Blue, Blue/Yellow, Yellow/Red, Red/Red and Yellow/Yellow
Nine ordered cartridge pair contracts, each in both HELLO orders
Same-hash Blue/Blue and Yellow/Yellow SaveRAM isolation through real Manager
Clean and approved UPR patching, genuine browser E2E and final artifact boots
Full native receptionist and durable physical trade matrix
Staged two-player human session after passing automation

requirements.description: All canonical capacities, layouts, names, PP/status encodings, endian rules, save geometry and checksum invariants

proofs.assertion_basis: 87 rows, 29 per pokered, pokeyellow and alchav_pokered, from the pinned source: capacities (PARTY_LENGTH, MONS_PER_BOX, NUM_BOXES, NUM_MOVES, MAX_LEVEL, MAX_STAT_VALUE, BAG_ITEM_CAPACITY), layouts (box, party and battle macro members against symbols, the 66-byte transfer blob, OTID, Exp and base-stat offsets, four name strides, six contiguous stat stages), names (NAME_LENGTH, the $50 terminator, the $FF species terminator), PP_UP_MASK, PP_MASK and the PSN, BRN, FRZ, PAR and SLP status masks, big-endian computed stats, SRAM box, bank, main-save and flag geometry with save-copy ranges, and the checksum invariants (complemented byte sum, the sGameData span, checksum adjacency, per-bank box checksums); growth curves are checked against the Lua data.
Regenerates the safe name alphabet, the PP of 165 moves and 151 species facts per title from the canonical builds and compares both published artifacts (the names clause).
Negative control: a one-byte party_struct symbol drift makes the validator emit FAIL, so the 87 OK rows are not vacuous.

The multibyte codec and min-level enforcement that canonical.structure-limits defers here: level 0 (and the siblings for level or box level 101) is refused by both the Python and the Lua codec without mutating the blob; test_all_canonical_species_at_level_boundaries_agree_between_codecs checks 151 species at four levels with multibyte experience, stat experience and computed stats agreeing across codecs.

The Lua SRAM box checksum writer reproduces the complemented byte sum of the source over scattered non-zero content for bank 2 (the sibling covers bank 3), tying the checksum invariant to runtime behaviour.

requirements.description: Every hook, free span, bank-qualified call, protected header byte, UPR pointer root and payload is source and byte validated
Per-title maps/subareas, every encounter method, types, moves, trainers, items, gifts, statics and evolution families match canonical source
Complete selected unit inventory passes without skip or expected failure

proofs.assertion_basis: Runs a real pytest subprocess with the release plugin and asserts validate_pytest_report reports problems for a skipped test even though stdout claims 999 passed (the without-skip clause of the unit inventory).
Real subprocess evidence for an xfail-marked test is rejected (the without-expected-failure clause).
A non-strict XPASS is rejected as evidence, so an expected-failure marker cannot pass the gate either way.
A module-level collection skip is rejected, so a selected file cannot leave the inventory by skipping itself.

proofs.nodeid:
tests/unit/test_gen1_release_gate.py::test_actual_pytest_reports_reject_nonpassing_outcomes[def test_case():
    assert True
def test_omitted():
    assert True
-args6-False]
proofs.assertion_basis: Deselecting one selected test with -k fails the report although every executed test passed (the complete-selected-inventory clause).

validate_pytest_report reports inventory drift when an expected node id is absent from a fully passing report; test_complete_current_execution_passes is the positive control. Together with the four proofs above this is the gate policy the row describes: the unit check passes only when the complete selected inventory executes with no skip or expected failure.

requirements.description: Partial receive/send offsets, queue bounds, reconnect replay and dispatcher/deferred exceptions with explicit NACK and continued processing

proofs.assertion_basis: Drives lua/connector.lua with a socket that accepts partial sends and asserts the next pump resumes at the exact absolute byte offset (partial send offsets).
A line delivered across several receive fragments is reassembled exactly once (partial receive offsets).
send returns false at the queue bound, nothing is dropped and sending resumes after drain; test_receive_backpressure_bounds_memory_without_losing_order covers the inbound bound (queue bounds).

After close, reopen and fresh hellos, resending the original operation_id yields no new events and identical pending outboxes with the rules unchanged (reconnect replay); test_durable_dispatch.py::test_v2_operation_survives_new_session_and_server_restart_without_repeating_rules asserts the same across a new session-gate epoch.

Real dispatch_commands from the client: an injected handler error produces an explicit NACK and a command_nack event, and the following hud_show still executes (dispatcher exception with explicit NACK and continued processing).

An injected validator exception leaves the pending sync queue empty and writes at zero, NACKs, and the next command runs; server side, test_gen1_runtime_server.py::test_unexpected_domain_exception_nacks_and_revokes_without_partial_rules asserts NACK over real TCP with journal rules unchanged.

Deferred-executor exceptions: a source pin that the deferred sync executor block is wrapped in pcall, and test_gen1_nacks_a_failed_sync_command_before_dropping_it pins that its failure branch emits sync_retrieve_failed or memorialize_failed. This clause is source-pinned, not executed; the executed evidence for the row is the dispatcher-level pair above.

requirements.description: Exact per-player final hash, profile, provenance, codec, capabilities, nonce and epoch gating before every semantic/write operation

proofs.assertion_basis: A hello whose final_rom_sha1 differs from the per-player contract is NACKed with no commands, and player identity, rom type, adapter, party caches, sessions and connected players are byte-identical before and after (exact per-player final hash).

The same zero-mutation NACK for a wrong content profile hash; the sibling parameters content_profile_schema-old, party_codec-old and patch_version-3 cover profile, codec and provenance, capabilities-value8 and value9 cover capabilities, client_nonce-bad covers the nonce.
Capabilities that do not match the contract profile exactly are refused before any state is adopted.
An admitted player whose semantic event carries a stale admission_epoch is NACKed and the player area does not change (epoch gating before a semantic operation).
Rewriting rom_contract.json rotates the epoch, NACKs the in-flight event, clears both sessions and de-admits both players without a new hello.

Through SLinkServer._dispatch a rejected hello returns only noop, never queues a box_mon write, and leaves player identity, trainer names and rom type unset; the sibling test_a_non_hello_event_from_an_unadmitted_player_is_dropped asserts a capture from an unadmitted player records no pending capture or link (gating before every semantic and write operation).

requirements.description: Durable operation IDs, session sequences, ACK/NACK, zero-mutation validation and collision checks on every key-producing operation

proofs.assertion_basis: A repeated operation_id returns the original receipt, the revision stays at 1, outboxes are not duplicated, and reusing the id with a different payload raises JournalError (durable operation ids).
Session nonces are durable across reopen and unique per player; state and outboxes are untouched by refused registrations (session sequences).

A skipped seq on the live session is NACKed with no semantic change; change0 (seq reuse) and test_duplicate_retries_return_original_response_without_redispatch (an identical retry is served from the journal, a conflicting retry is NACKed, _dispatch never re-runs) complete the session-sequence clause.
acknowledge persists an explicit NACK once, refuses a conflicting proof, and the pending outbox reflects it after reopen; the ACK parameter mirrors it.
A refused commit leaves the snapshot state, the event lookup and both outboxes exactly as before (zero-mutation validation).

_handle_capture raises AmbiguousPhysicalKey and _handle_key_change refuses a collision on a duplicated key with the staged document unchanged; test_gen1_identity_and_collisions.py::test_a_capture_colliding_with_a_live_link_is_refused and ::test_index_entry_refuses_same_save_aliasing cover link-time and index-time collisions (collision checks on key-producing operations).

requirements.description: Rule engine and persistence through actual server routes and APIs

proofs.assertion_basis: Real asyncio TCP into SLinkServer.handle_client with the legacy dispatch forbidden: a faint over the wire is ACKed, the first link becomes DEAD in the rule engine, the partner receives gen1_hold, and sessions close on disconnect.
aiohttp TestClient on build_app: /api/status returns 200, /api/reset 409, /launcher/a.lua 400, and the journal snapshot is unchanged afterward (persistence through actual HTTP routes).
Over real TCP an unconfigured durable hello is NACKed with reason code gen1_durable_runtime_unconfigured and state.to_document is unchanged.

Real TCP: a pre-hello event is NACKed, an oversize line is NACKed and a hello then ACKs on the same socket, a second-player hello on the wrong socket is NACKed, a replacement connection is admitted and the old close does not evict it.

A Manager POST to /api/attempts proxied into a live run app sets the attempts count and persists it to links.json; a cross-site origin gets 403 and the file bytes are unchanged (persistence through actual routes).

requirements.description: Gen 1 accurate UI, safe JSON, stream active-run pins, capability-gated controls and variant labels
Existing Archipelago behavior and gates remain safe; all inherited new R/B fields nil or independently verified

proofs.assertion_basis: Over real TCP a red_ap hello is admitted, returns a config command, binds game_id gen1_rby with is_rr false and a later tick is accepted; the blue_ap parameter mirrors it (existing Archipelago behaviour).
operation_decision for reset stays available on a red_ap-bound server, so the vanilla-RBY handler restrictions do not leak onto Archipelago (gates remain safe).
StagedGen1State.from_live refuses a red_ap state as not vanilla RBY, keeping Archipelago on its existing persistence path.
Injecting a new field into the red profile of lua/games/gen1_rby.lua leaves it absent from the effective red_ap and blue_ap profiles (inherited new R/B fields are nil).

Every effective field of red_ap and blue_ap has a verifier row with severity OK against the alchav_pokered symbols (independently verified); test_gen1_archipelago.py::test_ap_profile_uses_relocated_addresses pins the relocated deltas explicitly. Needs the pinned pret sources present, which the gate requires.

requirements.description: Canonical MoveMon/RemovePokemon/party and box compaction/append from cloned emulator states; all counts, slots, boundary failures, stats/level derivation, HP/status, names/species lists, dex changes, SRAM bank/checksum and immediate reload persistence

proofs.assertion_basis: On the live Red cartridge, lua/tests/test_gen1_storage_differential.lua runs the cartridge's own _MoveMon/_RemovePokemon through a RAM trampoline on a cloned core state and compares SLink's depositPartyMon/retrieveBoxMon against it over the authoritative ranges (party and box counts, species lists, structs, OT and nickname arrays, dex owned/seen, current box, SRAM bank): 400 deposit/party-compaction cases (party 2..6, box 0..19, every slot), 1260 withdraw/box-compaction/append cases (party 0..5, box 1..20, every slot), and a stale BoxLevel case proving the level is derived from experience; the comparator is proven to detect a one-byte mutation. Covers counts, slots, compaction/append, HP/status, names/species lists and dex changes.

Boundary failures on the live Red cartridge, lua/tests/test_gen1_storage_boundaries.lua: depositPartyMon refuses the last party member (box 0/10/19), a full current box (party 2 and 6, every slot) and an invalid slot (-1, count, 6, 1.5, a string, true, nil); retrieveBoxMon refuses a full party (box 1 and 20); each refusal returns the production message and the whole WRAM (C000-DFFF), HRAM and 32 KB SRAM image plus the SRAM bank register are byte-identical before and after (the comparator is proven on a one-byte SRAM and a one-byte WRAM mutation); positive controls one past each boundary succeed so the refusals are not vacuous.

Stats and level derivation on the live Red cartridge: canonical CalcExperience and CalcStats run unchanged with bank-qualified symbols on cloned core states and SLink's derivation is compared against them.

SRAM bank/checksum and immediate reload persistence on the live Red cartridge: canonical SRAM initialization for all 12 current-box values matches the cartridge's EmptyAllSRAMBoxes plus SaveMainData image byte for byte across the whole 32 KB (tails retained), initialization is idempotent, a normal deposit followed by a memorial matches the canonical SaveCurrentBoxData then SavePartyAndDexData image, the canonical loaders and the ChangeBox first-time branch retain the grave, and a real core reset (client.reboot_core) reaches CONTINUE with the initialized bit, the grave, the party and the boxed mon intact.

requirements.description: Live proof of the adopted write-safe predicate; no proof keeps writes disabled

proofs.assertion_basis: lua/tests/test_gen1_write_safety_overworld.lua samples the production memory_gb isPartyWriteSafe predicate every frame under ROM exec hooks on Red: a positive idle candidate exists in the overworld; twelve START-menu rows with and without the Pokedex, the real Pokemon Center PC (Withdraw, Deposit, Release, ChangeBox selectors, the stats screen, the twelve-box selector), the cable-club handshake and a poison blackout each assert no non-world candidate (EnterMap, DisplayTextID, naming and PC contexts) and that a writable checkpoint is regained; reset and title never qualify. This is the live proof of the adopted write-safe predicate across the overworld, transition, menu, PC, blackout, reset and title axes.

lua/tests/test_gen1_write_safety_battle.lua boots the Red battle fixture through CONTINUE, starts a real wild battle, captures with a Master Ball into DisplayNamingScreen and returns to the overworld; asserts that boot, battle and naming were sampled and never qualify (isPartyWriteSafe false on every sampled frame) and that positive world control qualifies. Covers the battle, naming and boot axes of the predicate.

requirements.description: Active box WRAM plus eleven SRAM boxes, invalid current box refusal, recomputed withdrawn stats, initialized bit/checksum before memorial, whole empty reserved box, NACK and canonical initiator deposit undo

proofs.assertion_basis: Active box WRAM plus eleven SRAM boxes: storedBoxKeys reads the current box from WRAM and the other eleven from their SRAM bank offsets, refuses an invalid current box, and before the first ChangeBox reports only the current box (test_inactive_boxes_do_not_exist_before_first_changebox); the same scan is what the live memorial proof walks across the party and all twelve boxes.

On the live Red cartridge, lua/tests/test_gen1_storage_boundaries.lua: invalid current box refusal, wCurrentBoxNum in {12, 13, 127, $8C, $8D, $FF} makes both depositPartyMon and retrieveBoxMon return the production refusal with WRAM/HRAM/SRAM and the bank register byte-identical, while 11, $8B, 0 and $80 are legal and deposit succeeds; whole empty reserved box, a live record hidden at reserved-box slot 0, 7 or 19 past a zero count refuses depositMemorialMon with no byte changed, and a dead tail record at slot 19 is left untouched by a successful memorial that writes only slot 0 of the struct, OT and nickname arrays, with boxes 7..11 of the memorial bank byte-identical; canonical initiator deposit undo, after the cartridge's own MoveMon deposit (party 2..6, box 0/5/18, every slot: 60 cases) retrieveBoxMon of the deposited key reproduces the cartridge's inverse MoveMon withdraw on a cloned state over the authoritative ranges and restores both counts, and after a canonical withdrawal (18 cases) depositPartyMon reproduces the cartridge's inverse deposit.

Recomputed withdrawn stats on the live Red cartridge: a no-cache retrieval recomputes and appends, the received mon lands behind the untouched original, all 33 boxed bytes and 22 name bytes survive, the level is recomputed instead of replaying a stale BoxLevel, a middle-box removal compacts both records and the parallel names, unavailable canonical evidence NACKs without writes and restored evidence permits retry.

Initialized bit and checksum before memorial on the live Red cartridge: protectSramBoxes reproduces the cartridge's EmptyAllSRAMBoxes plus SaveMainData image for every current box, persists the initialization flag and its covering checksum, and the memorial poststate equals the canonical current-box then party/dex save.

NACK and canonical initiator undo, server side: an invalid partner box selector or an unsafe peer read never writes the peer and restores the initiator; a cartridge deposit refusal (full box, Yellow restriction) keeps the peer's containers and undoes the actor; an observed deposit synchronizes or canonically undoes after the verified peer read for every title pairing (sibling parametrizations).

The per-player final hash is the clean profile final_rom_sha1 carried in each HELLO (admission.cartridge_metadata); its gating is asserted by the second proof.
A HELLO whose final_rom_sha1 does not match the contract is refused (NACK) and leaves rule identity and the cartridge caches unchanged, so admission is gated on the exact per-player final hash.

requirements.description: A refused outbound frame does not consume Gen1 sequence/response bookkeeping; post-battle safe notifications survive disconnection, busy states and a full queue.

proofs.assertion_basis: Actual client fragments refuse to consume a sequence/response label on backpressure and retain safe notifications until a send queues successfully.

requirements.description: Real x64 LuaSocket DLL exchanges multibyte long frames across read/send boundaries, receives 1000 ordered replies under deliberate backpressure, rejects an oversized frame through its delimiter, drops a stale complete response and reconnects to a nonce-bound fresh stream. No semantic replay or admission is claimed.

proofs.assertion_basis: Independent local TCP peer verifies exact outbound bytes and a fresh reconnect ACK. Emulator asserts exact inbound byte content, 1000-line ordering, all buffer bounds and the per-pump send budget with a live queue peak of 128.

requirements.description: Malformed keys, stats, display values and collections refuse before queue/cache/HUD mutation; validation and handler exceptions generate NACKs and later valid commands still execute. Durable ACK delivery is separately required.

Native/host/closure evidence is modeled; real receptionist/executor binding and ordinary execution remain open. Both exact admitted cartridges must expose PC trade and the matching codec; any unpatched participant refuses even when a physical policy is supplied. Positive host/native evidence remains modeled.

Identical Kanto starters under the species lock: the bridge surfaces the engine rejection ({player, key, reason}); no link, the first half stays pending with the lab waiting on the rejected player, the rejected key is unusable and retry-listed, and no dangling commands, memorial or Pokeball credit remain.
Yellow/Yellow: two Pikachu starters link ALIVE as the one exempt gift.
A mixed pair applies the clauses and Pikachu never collides with Bulbasaur, Charmander or Squirtle: every mixed pairing links.

Shared engine via gen1_semantic_events.faint_event: the linked death marks the pair DEAD at the reported level, queues the partner's force_faint and memorialize and returns the caller's own memorialize.
Under explode_mode with the Gen 1 adapter the partner command is force_explode, never force_faint.

A faint before Pokeballs are obtained leaves the link ALIVE and queues no partner command.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_ambiguous_same_player_key_refuses_without_selecting_a_pair case (the detached rule helpers of linked_death_rules/party_grant_rules were folded into the shared engine: gen1_engine_bridge feeds gen1_semantic_events to SoulLinkState.handle_event). update_run_over (the one rule helper left beside the engine): seed_link_half pends the first half and links the second with no queued commands or Pokeball credit; the run is over only with both balls, no live pair and no unproved ball.

requirements.description: Real journal atomically stores and replays free-run observation batches: the progress row equals its journal record, a skipped or repeated sequence or a backwards frame refuses without a commit, replaying the same operation returns the committed result without a second commit, hostile or unenrolled batches commit nothing, and a SQL failure inside the inventory commit rolls the whole transaction back; removing retained native-loan grant history refuses on state load. Free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode; no ordinary frame grant exists.

proofs.assertion_basis: Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_corrupt_frame_record_refuses_even_when_snapshot_is_unchanged case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). Deleting a retained native grant history record makes runtime.state() refuse even after a later valid return: the ledger's provenance records are immutable authority.

Free-run observation batches (gen1_observation_runtime.record) must carry a contiguous sequence and a monotonic frame: a skipped or repeated sequence or a backwards frame raises JournalError with the journal snapshot unchanged; the committed progress row equals its journal record for that player only and verify_journal passes.

Re-delivering the same observation operation (fresh transport seq, same semantic event) returns the committed reply without a second commit; record() replays the committed result (inventory transition digest and observation digest) and a replay with different semantic content is refused with the snapshot unchanged.

A heartbeat inventory inside a batch records the checkpoint through the real inventory-observation handler: sequence, previous_operation_id chained to the previous batch operation, transition (party_hp_zero) and record history; the result carries the inventory transition digest and no deferral; verify_journal passes and the components survive reopen.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_sql_record_failure_never_publishes_half_a_frame_transition[enroll] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: enrollment.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_sql_record_failure_never_publishes_half_a_frame_transition[grant] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: shape.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_sql_record_failure_never_publishes_half_a_frame_transition[return] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A SQL failure inserting the inventory record rolls back rules, identity and link together: one identity, no link, snapshot unchanged.

requirements.description: Observation batches are bound to the enrolled context: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape or an unenrolled player refuses without a commit; the sequence must be contiguous and frames monotonic; a heartbeat checkpoint stays deferred while any physical obligation is open; a native-loan (frame-accounted) player cannot publish standalone observations and its handoff checkpoint refuses a forged identity, replaced host or missing inventory; a native return cannot adopt ungranted frames. This binding grants no production gameplay.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: identity.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: owner.

A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: shape.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: missing_inventory.

A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: enrollment.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: extra_frames.

While any physical obligation is open (a published force_faint, then its memorial obligations) a heartbeat checkpoint in a batch is deferred: the result says inventory_deferred and carries no transition digest, the inventory sequence does not advance, and verify_journal passes.

requirements.description: Semantic evidence inside an observation batch resolves to its containing committed event: revision, result digests and command ids; a changed entry or observation refuses and a foreign player resolves nothing; standalone receipts keep replay semantics. Native loans retain their grant history: removed history refuses on load, a return cannot adopt ungranted or foreign progress or a wrong challenge, sequence or receipt digest, renewal spends only granted capacity and the handoff query is read-only; tampered settled records refuse on restore; malformed acquisition rows and batch shapes refuse without publication. Real SQLite with synthetic Yellow/Yellow enrollment; no ordinary gameplay permission.

proofs.assertion_basis: Engine and inventory entries staged by one observation batch carry the batch operation id and no frame_origin; semantic_receipt resolves each to the outer committed event (revision, ack, its evidence digest, ordinary_execution false, command ids) and the batch result carries the same digests.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: changed-entry.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: changed-observation.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: foreign-player.
A standalone engine_signals event keeps its receipt lookup: semantic_receipt returns the committed EventReceipt and reusing the operation id with a changed request is refused ('reused').
Deleting a retained native grant history record makes runtime.state() refuse even after a later valid return: the ledger's provenance records are immutable authority.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: challenge.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: receipt.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: wrong_count.
A second native command cannot be granted until the previous frame-return is acknowledged ('previous frame-return'); the journal is unchanged.
An acceptance frame beyond the old grant's range refuses the return ('granted range') with the journal unchanged.
Credits spent between a renewal request and its acceptance are charged to the old grant: the closed receipt spans acceptance to return and the total steps equal both grants' spending.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_malformed_window_is_journal_refusal_without_publication[None] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A native grant renewal retires the unused capacity of the prior grant (pending 'before' moves to the request frame), replaying persist_grant changes nothing, the ordinary frame-progress baseline stays frozen while borrowed, and the return advances the native progress to the returned frame.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_malformed_window_is_journal_refusal_without_publication[window1] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). The native handoff readiness query is read-only (snapshot unchanged) and binds the return operation reference.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_malformed_window_is_journal_refusal_without_publication[window2] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). After both players' returns an active trade blocks the handoff transition ('transaction'); each handoff is replay-safe, moves the ordinary ledger frame to the returned frame with no pending observation, both checkpoints become candidates, and a later loan borrows exactly where the handoff left the ledger.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_invalid_name_in_held_bundle_is_journal_refusal_without_closure[5050505050505050505050-inventory] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). Acquisition observation replay returns the committed result without a second commit; restore rechecks evidence: a tampered settled fact refuses verify_journal (atomic record / authoritative receipt), altered ordinals and a wrong pairing key refuse verify_state.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_invalid_name_in_held_bundle_is_journal_refusal_without_closure[5050505050505050505050-engine] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). Re-delivering the same observation operation (fresh transport seq, same semantic event) returns the committed reply without a second commit; record() replays the committed result (inventory transition digest and observation digest) and a replay with different semantic content is refused with the snapshot unchanged.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_invalid_name_in_held_bundle_is_journal_refusal_without_closure[0050505050505050505050-inventory] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: kind.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_invalid_name_in_held_bundle_is_journal_refusal_without_closure[0050505050505050505050-engine] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). requirements.description: Starter source and stable checkpoint settle through observation batches into one paired link; a faint signal carried by a batch settles exactly as the standalone engine event and publishes the partner force-faint atomically with the death record; an acquisition receipt settles pending or in the same batch as its checkpoint; a SQL failure in the inventory commit rolls back rules, identity and link together; a real death recorded while storage compensation is open waits for it. Source and physical observations are synthetic; no ordinary runtime permission is inferred.

proofs.assertion_basis: A battle or poison faint signal carried inside an observation batch settles exactly as the standalone engine_signals event: identical death record (pending_faint, peer b), engine record transactions (pokeballs_obtained, faint), DEAD link, released party keys on both sides and the single partner force_faint command. Case: battle_faint.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_inventory_failure_rolls_back_source_rule_and_command_proposals case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A battle or poison faint signal carried inside an observation batch settles exactly as the standalone engine_signals event: identical death record (pending_faint, peer b), engine record transactions (pokeballs_obtained, faint), DEAD link, released party keys on both sides and the single partner force_faint command. Case: poison_faint.
A SQL failure inserting the inventory record rolls back rules, identity and link together: one identity, no link, snapshot unchanged.
Starter source signals and the stable checkpoint delivered as two observation batches per player settle both starters (sources, then settled) into one ALIVE link with no barrier ticket (R/Y pair).

An acquisition receipt in a batch stays pending until a checkpoint at or after its return frame and settles at once when receipt and checkpoint share one batch (inventory staged first); settled rows carry pairing key, area, no violation and the checkpoint batch operation; ordinals, the ALIVE link, verify_state/verify_journal and reopen agree.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_starter_sources_inventory_and_identity_close_in_one_frame_commit[variants2] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A real source faint observed while both storage reads are open is recorded (pending_issue) without publishing force_faint; the storage job aborts with the linked-death refusal, force_faint is issued only after both storage writes with the storage write as its origin (not the source event), a forged issuer or erased issuance refuses verify_journal, and the exact faint receipt moves the death to pending_memorial; reopen verifies. Case: False.

requirements.description: Observation batches and native frame handoffs are the containing events of engine and inventory semantic receipts: batched semantics resolve the outer revision, digests and command ids; a changed entry or observation refuses and a foreign player resolves nothing; a frame-accounted player needs a native handoff origin; an active trade blocks the handoff transition; a native return cannot adopt a wrong challenge, receipt or sequence; inventory-only batches carry no invented engine evidence; starter source and checkpoint settle through batches and settled acquisitions carry their checkpoint's batch operation; handoff checkpoints stage detached and refuse bad evidence. Synthetic frame and source evidence; no frame permission is granted by the reference.

proofs.assertion_basis: Engine and inventory entries staged by one observation batch carry the batch operation id and no frame_origin; semantic_receipt resolves each to the outer committed event (revision, ack, its evidence digest, ordinary_execution false, command ids) and the batch result carries the same digests.

After both players' returns an active trade blocks the handoff transition ('transaction'); each handoff is replay-safe, moves the ordinary ledger frame to the returned frame with no pending observation, both checkpoints become candidates, and a later loan borrows exactly where the handoff left the ledger.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: changed-entry.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: changed-observation.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: missing_inventory.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_forged_origin_or_closed_bundle_refuses_before_publication[no-closure] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). A second native command cannot be granted until the previous frame-return is acknowledged ('previous frame-return'); the journal is unchanged.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: challenge.

semantic_receipt refuses a changed entry (forged transactions) or a changed observation (moved frame) with 'free-run observation differs' and resolves nothing for a foreign player. Case: foreign-player.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: receipt.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: sequence.

A player whose ordinary ledger is seeded (frame-accounted) cannot publish standalone engine signals or an observation batch; stage_origin demands a native_frame_handoff containing event; observation_bundle extracts the handoff inventory with no engine signals and refuses a host frame that disagrees with the held source checkpoint.

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_frame_accounted_player_cannot_publish_standalone_observation[inventory_observation] case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). The native handoff readiness query is read-only (snapshot unchanged) and binds the return operation reference.

A heartbeat inventory inside a batch records the checkpoint through the real inventory-observation handler: sequence, previous_operation_id chained to the previous batch operation, transition (party_hp_zero) and record history; the result carries the inventory transition digest and no deferral; verify_journal passes and the components survive reopen.
Starter source signals and the stable checkpoint delivered as two observation batches per player settle both starters (sources, then settled) into one ALIVE link with no barrier ticket (R/Y pair).

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: identity.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: owner.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: battle.

Case: party.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: None.

Paired native checkpoints exist only after both native loans are handed back: each handoff records the checkpoint at the returned frame and its journal record; checkpoints() returns detached copies, candidate_checkpoints covers both players, verify_journal passes and the component survives reopen.
A standalone engine_signals event keeps its receipt lookup: semantic_receipt returns the committed EventReceipt and reusing the operation id with a changed request is refused ('reused').

Nearest surviving assertion for the retired test_valid_origin_allows_queued_commands_and_same_physical_reconnect case (the frame-credit loop and its compound-frame bundles are deleted; free-run observation batches are the only gameplay client mode). An acquisition receipt in a batch stays pending until a checkpoint at or after its return frame and settles at once when receipt and checkpoint share one batch (inventory staged first); settled rows carry pairing key, area, no violation and the checkpoint batch operation; ordinals, the ALIVE link, verify_state/verify_journal and reopen agree.

requirements.description: Observation batches carry only what the frame produced: the Lua loop publishes nothing on a quiet frame, signals without inventory on a signal frame and inventory alone on a heartbeat frame, appends before draining, lands sequence numbers in the baseline, services the writer only after publication, persists the capture cursor and fails closed on oversized batches without dropping; a signals-only batch settles exactly as the standalone engine event; the native frame handoff stages its checkpoint detached and refuses a forged identity, owner, battle state, party or missing inventory; open storage reads and writes defer the heartbeat checkpoint; unknown kinds and malformed shapes commit nothing; a native return cannot adopt extra, miscounted or foreign frames.

proofs.assertion_basis: The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: None.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: owner.

Lua loop (lua/gen1_observation_loop.lua) under stubbed BizHawk globals: a quiet non-heartbeat frame peeks, prepares, checks the writer, pumps and marks ready but appends and persists nothing; the cursor comes from observers:initial at the start frame and at_boundary is cleared afterwards.
Engine signals are batched and appended to the journal as one observation event (frame, signals, null inventory) before the engine queue and the observers drain; the queue is empty afterwards.

A heartbeat frame (every 30 frames) publishes the inventory with null signals and an empty acquisitions array, reads the inventory exactly once, never drains the engine, and the next quiet frame publishes nothing.

Each published event increments the observation sequence and the baseline records it; engine batches keep their own contiguous counter and the acquisition cursor frame lands in the persisted baseline.
The held writer is serviced only when it reports pending work, and only after the batch is appended and the engine drained, before the session pump.
The session is pumped on every tick regardless of publication (45 ticks, one heartbeat appended).

An oversized signal (33) or acquisition (17) batch raises the source-bounds LuaError before anything is appended or drained: refused, not dropped, and at_boundary is cleared. Case: signal-33-frame signal batch exceeds source bounds.

An oversized signal (33) or acquisition (17) batch raises the source-bounds LuaError before anything is appended or drained: refused, not dropped, and at_boundary is cleared. Case: receipt-17-frame acquisition batch exceeds source bounds.
A capture call witnessed without its receipt persists the acquisition cursor (capture_open, frame) before the observers drain, and the next prepare sees the moved cursor.
A persisted acquisition cursor in the baseline is adopted on start instead of calling observers:initial.
Without acquisition observers the loop still publishes signal batches with an empty acquisitions array and never calls prepare or ready.

Case: battle.

The native checkpoint inside a native_frame_handoff stages detached (entry frame/party equal the handoff, per-player record key, document updated, journal untouched) and refuses a forged save identity, a replaced host process, an in-battle readback, a forged party record or a missing inventory with no component written. Case: party.

Paired native checkpoints exist only after both native loans are handed back: each handoff records the checkpoint at the returned frame and its journal record; checkpoints() returns detached copies, candidate_checkpoints covers both players, verify_journal passes and the component survives reopen.

A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: kind.

A hostile observation batch commits nothing: a wrong ROM hash, context generation, physical instance or save identity, an unknown acquisition kind, a malformed shape, or a batch from an unenrolled player raises JournalError with the snapshot unchanged and no progress row. Case: shape.
Open storage reads and storage_apply writes defer the heartbeat checkpoint of an observation batch: inventory_deferred with no transition digest, and the recorded observation frame stays behind.

A battle or poison faint signal carried inside an observation batch settles exactly as the standalone engine_signals event: identical death record (pending_faint, peer b), engine record transactions (pokeballs_obtained, faint), DEAD link, released party keys on both sides and the single partner force_faint command. Case: battle_faint.

A battle or poison faint signal carried inside an observation batch settles exactly as the standalone engine_signals event: identical death record (pending_faint, peer b), engine record transactions (pokeballs_obtained, faint), DEAD link, released party keys on both sides and the single partner force_faint command. Case: poison_faint.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: extra_frames.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: wrong_count.

A native frame return cannot adopt extra ungranted frames, a miscounted step total, a foreign host owner, a wrong grant challenge, a skipped ledger sequence or a forged receipt digest: JournalError with the snapshot unchanged. Case: owner.
